rows.passage_en: Administrator-level malware can leave persistent changes such as backdoors. Ending the original process or rebooting does not necessarily remove the compromise; serious infections can require rebuilding the host from a known-clean state.
rows.review_note: Key says often, not necessarily always. Rebuilding supports the intended strongest offered recovery; disk wiping alone is not a universal guarantee against firmware or credential compromise. No implication every infection requires wiping.

rows.passage_en: Address Resolution Protocol lets a device obtain a link-layer hardware address corresponding to a network-layer protocol address, such as mapping an IPv4 address to an Ethernet address on a local network.
rows.review_note: Keep distinction from DNS host-name to IP mapping. This is local-network resolution, not Internet-wide hardware discovery.

rows.source_locator: Why use pimpl and Pimpl header
rows.passage_en: A pointer to a hidden implementation keeps an object’s public layout independent of the size of its private implementation. Changing that implementation can avoid rebuilding clients, at the cost of an extra pointer access.
rows.review_note: Conventional unoptimized representation comparison: direct layout avoids indirection; a hidden allocated implementation provides a compilation firewall. Neither automatically requires a noticeable compilation-time increase.

rows.source_locator: What Makes Pipelining Hard; Complex Instructions; multi-cycle operations
rows.passage_en: Instruction decoding with variable lengths, implicit condition-code dependencies, and operations with very different execution times complicate a pipeline. Merely organizing registers into separate sets does not itself impose those sequencing problems.
rows.review_note: Source explicitly covers condition codes and multi-cycle complexity. Variable-length decoding and register-set comparison are architectural reasoning and need specific final supporting passages before approval.

rows.source_locator: MAP_SHARED versus MAP_PRIVATE; independent address-offset calculation
rows.passage_en: Mappings of the same backing storage can begin at different virtual addresses. Shared writable mappings propagate writes to that storage; a private copy-on-write mapping instead isolates later modifications.
rows.review_note: Offset77E81234-77E80000=1234hex; debugger mapping01000000+1234=01001234. A needs write access/shared underlying text; B copy-on-write would not modify P. Background virtual address translation also in OSTEP vm-intro.

rows.source_locator: Microprogrammed Control: horizontal versus vertical microinstructions
rows.passage_en: Horizontal microinstructions expose control signals directly, allowing several compatible micro-operations in a cycle. Vertical microinstructions encode more of the control information and require decoding.
rows.review_note: Educational convention: unencoded horizontal control, not a claim every real implementation has literally no encoded field. Does not imply horizontal needs more steps or a single opcode like an ordinary machine instruction.

rows.source_locator: A Unique Opportunity to See the Corona; Modern Observations
rows.passage_en: The solar corona is a tenuous plasma whose visible light is much fainter than the photosphere. Blocking the bright solar disk during a total eclipse makes the faint corona visible to the unaided eye.
rows.review_note: Prompt overstates except-eclipse because instruments/coronagraphs can also observe it; use naked-eye context implicit in introductory astronomy. Diffuse/faint is intendedD, not cold or nonluminous.

rows.source_locator: Saturn interior/gravitational compression; independent comparative interpretation
rows.passage_en: Self-gravity compresses giant-planet material, increasing its density. A larger mass can therefore produce a much smaller proportional increase in radius than would occur if density stayed fixed.
rows.review_note: Cassini source explains pressure/gravitational compression; NASAFAQ gives Saturn84%Jupiterdiameter30%mass. The stronger specific causal comparison Jupiter/Saturn still needs final adjudication of composition contributions, not mere density arithmetic.

rows.source_locator: Atmosphere; comparison to other giant-planet atmosphere pages
rows.passage_en: The giant planets have hydrogen-rich outer atmospheres, with helium and smaller amounts of other gases. Methane is a much smaller atmospheric component than hydrogen in Uranus and Neptune.
rows.review_note: The question does not specify atmosphere versus bulk elemental abundance or number versus mass. This source is atmospheric evidence only; do not approve as a bulk-composition proof without checking that distinction.

rows.passage_en: Methane can condense into clouds under sufficiently cold conditions. In the ice giants, gaseous methane also absorbs red light and contributes to their blue-green appearance.
rows.review_note: NASA page supports methane/color, not the full cloud-condensation contrast with Jupiter/Saturn. Draft needs a direct cloud-temperature source before final approval; avoid conflating blue color with blue methane ice itself.

rows.passage_en: The Large Magellanic Cloud is a small satellite galaxy associated with the Milky Way, containing stars, gas clouds, and active star-forming regions.
rows.review_note: NASA explicitly calls it a satellite galaxy and a small irregular galaxy; not a planetary nebula or a single star cluster. Orbital first-infall refinements do not change category.

rows.passage_en: When light with a continuous spectrum passes through cooler gas, the gas absorbs particular wavelengths characteristic of its atoms. The transmitted spectrum retains the continuum with dark absorption lines superimposed.
rows.review_note: In this simplified setup cool hydrogen imprints hydrogen absorption lines; real stellar spectra also contain intrinsic lines. Does not turn the transmitted spectrum into pure emission.

rows.passage_en: All points of a rigid disk rotating about a fixed axis share the same angular displacement and rotation period. Their linear speeds differ with distance from the axis, according to v=r*omega.
rows.review_note: Point exactly on the axis has no circular path; intended comparison is material at nonzero radii. Standard rigid solid-disk model; not differential rotation of gaseous disks.

rows.passage_en: Nebular formation starts from a rotating disk of gas and dust, with planet formation influenced by temperature and available material. That picture does not impose a rule that rocky and giant planets must occur in equal numbers.
rows.review_note: NASA describes collapse, disk, and temperature-dependent materials. Negative fixed-number claim is model reasoning, not a published exact solution; final source check should address residual small bodies and impactors in other options.
